1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2.strategy: Completes the fianchetto: the bishop backs the e4 pawn and stands ready to hit the centre and the queenside along the long diagonal if the e-pawn ever advances or is exchanged. White chooses a slow build-up, and until then the bishop stays behind its own pawn.

1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2 Bg7.strategy: The same set-up for Black: the bishop attacks the c3 knight along the long diagonal and covers the dark squares. Both sides now have solid, matching structures, and the fight is about who breaks out first and where, White on the kingside, Black on the queenside.
